lessons.title: Masked subset gradient contribution under full-batch reduction denominator is not equivalent to an independently normalized subset loss gradient
lessons.description: Under PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='mean'), evaluating loss on an isolated class subset yields L_isolated = sum_{i in M} w_{y_i} ell_i / sum_{i in M} w_{y_i}. This causes two critical scientific failures: (1) for any single-class mask (e.g. M_c), w_c cancels identically from numerator and denominator, rendering weighted and uniform losses mathematically identical; and (2) the sum of isolated subset gradients does not equal the full-batch loss gradient (g_rare + g_common + g_other != g_total) because each subset divides by a different scalar denominator. Only by evaluating the masked gradient contribution under the full-batch reduction denominator D_batch = sum_{i in B_valid} w_{y_i} is exact linear decomposition preserved (g_total = sum g_{M_k}) and class-weight scaling w_c / bar{w}_batch retained. Subgradient protocols must explicitly report Estimand A ('masked gradient contribution under the full-batch reduction denominator') and prohibit calling it an unadorned class-specific loss gradient.

lessons.title: AdamW parameter update magnitude is governed by adaptive moments and decoupled weight decay, not directly by raw gradient L2 norm

The raw gradient L2 norm directly determines only whether global gradient clipping activates under torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(max_norm=1.0). lessons.title: Raw L2 norm and RMS per-parameter scale serve distinct roles and must not be conflated when comparing modules of different parameter counts

lessons.title: Small-sample (n=3) non-significant differences must not be interpreted as proof of no effect or grounds to reject an optimization bottleneck
lessons.description: With only n=3 paired random seeds, statistical power to detect small or moderate differences is inherently low, p-values are unstable, and inter-seed variance can mask real effects. lessons.title: Paired inference on within-batch subgradient geometry must aggregate to parent acquisition clusters to prevent batch-level pseudo-replication
lessons.description: In OPS-02 TRAIN, all 40 parent acquisition clusters contain between 2 and 4 physical tiles, and 17 clusters contain multiple tiles with dual-class support. lessons.title: Raw physical observations for cluster-level paired inference must be cluster-pure to prevent non-identifiable multi-cluster batch mixing

lessons.title: Execution authorization compute ceilings must be mathematically reconciled with deterministic scientific population requirements to prevent population truncation or execution failure
lessons.description: In DIAG-05, earlier design drafts using a 2-class common subset (MCC and IWs) identified 11 dual-supported 4-tile minibatches, corresponding to 44 H2 backward passes and 110 total passes within a 120-pass ceiling. When the protocol transitioned to the authoritative 7-class dynamic phenomena set (Common-7) and cluster-pure tile observations (LL-DIAG05-PLAN-024), the eligible Population-A count expanded to exactly 28 physical tiles across 15 parent clusters. Evaluating 28 tiles with 4 backward passes per tile (rare and common gradients across Control and Treatment arms) deterministically requires 112 H2 backward passes. Adding the 66 H1 census passes yields exactly 178 deterministic backward passes. Retaining a stale ceiling of 120 backward passes creates an operational contradiction: either the execution runner aborts upon exceeding the ceiling, or it is forced into unauthorized ad-hoc subsampling that discards more than half of the eligible population. Execution compute ceilings must be derived directly from the exact population census and pass mechanics, with ceilings strictly >= deterministic requirements.
